  • This includes the town council for Cork, Ireland, barring Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu from entering its city limits, citing his "illegal occupation of Palestine and bordering countries" and the continuous pro-Palestinian protests taking place every Saturday since October 2023, organized by the Cork Palestine Solidarity Campaign (CPSC).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two people were arrested by Irish police after agitators gathered at Trinity College Dublin while former President Joe Biden made a surprise visit on Tuesday (Credit: Credit: PA Media via Reuters).

In a recent development, the European hometown of the man who single-handedly destroyed a U.S. military transport aircraft in an act of apparent protest has a rich history of pro-Palestinian support.

This includes the town council for Cork, Ireland, barring Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu from entering its city limits, citing his "illegal occupation of Palestine and bordering countries" and the continuous pro-Palestinian protests taking place every Saturday since October 2023, organized by the Cork Palestine Solidarity Campaign (CPSC).

Cork’s opposition to Israel adds context to the possible motives for why Daithí O’Corráin, an Irish national, allegedly destroyed a U.S. military C-130 Hercules aircraft in April. The incident also draws attention to several anti-Israel groups that have sprung up in Ireland in recent years.

IRELAND’S ELITES HAVE FOUND THEIR NEW RELIGION: HATING ISRAEL.

Industry observers note that pro-Palestinian activists from the Ireland Palestine Solidarity Campaign, supported by members of left-wing parties including People Before Profit and the Socialist Party and students, participate in the National March for Palestine from the Garden of Remembrance to O'Connell Street and Leinster House, on May 18, 2024, in Dublin, Ireland. (Artur Widak/NurPhoto via Getty Images).

Ireland’s anti-Israel foothold became international news in April when O’Corráin, a Cork native, barricaded himself inside a C-130, a U.S. military transport plane. Once inside, he tore out critical wiring, destroyed gauges, contaminated fuel tanks and even poured corrosive chemicals into the aircraft, according to the U.S. Department of Justice.

According to recent reports, although his motives remain unclear, several groups from Cork interpreted his actions as a form of resistance against Israel and U.S. military interventionism.

Industry observers note that in one such case, a Cork business owner named Tracey Ryan released an initiative to raise €20,000 for O’Corráin's legal defense, praising his efforts to resist "the unwanted presence of U.S. military in Ireland in the face of their illegal war & support of Israel’s genocide.".

Recent findings suggest that "We, Daithí's friends and comrades, are raising funds to support him through his court case. We would really appreciate your support & will keep you updated here on ways to support Daithí," Ryan wrote in the description of the fundraising page.

According to her personal Facebook profile, Ryan joined a bus of pro-Palestinian activists who went to support O’Corráin at his court appearance. "Bus going to the high court to support Daithí on Thursday!!" Ryan wrote.

O’Corráin has also received support from CPSC, the Cork pro-Palestinian group.

As news of the incident spread, CPSC co-chair Anne McShane posted on her Palestinian advocacy Facebook page in support of O’Corráin, encouraging viewers to send him letters of encouragement after his incarceration.

"Daithi needs our support in order to keep up his morale. Letters are a lifeline for prisoners," an April 17 post read.

It has been revealed that CPSC spearheads anti-Israel demonstrations in Cork. In addition to hosting several pro-Palestinian fundraising initiatives, the group facilitates weekly Saturday demonstrations and invites speakers. At one point, CPSC’s website featured a fundraising site for O’Corráin, but the page has since been removed.

INSIDE THE PROTEST PLAYBOOK TO VILIFY ISRAEL ON 'GLOBAL DAY OF ACTION'.

Left: Smashed cockpit instruments inside a U.S. military C-130H Hercules aircraft allegedly destroyed at Shannon Airport in Ireland on April 11, 2026. Right: A separate U.S. Air Force C-130 Hercules aircraft at RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire, England, on March 18, 2026. (U.S. Department of Justice; Leon Neal/Getty Images).

In CPSC’s own words, the group is part of a larger pro-Palestinian movement.

"It’s not just the city. Towns across all of County Cork stand in solidarity with Palestinians, including Ballincollig, Bandon, Cobh, Charleville, Clonakilty, Fermoy, Kinsale, Macroom, Mallow, Mitchelstown, Skibbereen and more," the group states on its website.

"Cork Palestine Solidarity Campaign is a branch of the Irish Palestine Solidarity Campaign (IPSC)," it added.

As part of its sister groups’ efforts "to foster links between Palestine and Irish institutions and organizations," CPSC and IPSC have both applauded Cork’s city council efforts to promote pro-Palestinian policies.

"Well done to the Cork City Council which passed a motion … calling for the Central Bank to end the sale of Israeli bonds," one Facebook post reads.

The groups have also held Cork up as a template for Ireland’s national policy.

"We call on the Irish government to follow the example of both Dublin and Cork city councils by officially recognizing Israeli Apartheid – and acting to end any and all links to this regime," another statement reads.

For its own part, the Cork City Council has earned the support of IPSC and CPSC through a range of its official resolutions, making the town’s formal position to condemn any of Ireland’s ties to Israel.

In addition to banning Netanyahu from entering the city's limits in a 41-8 vote in 2024, Cork’s council has flown the Palestinian flag over city hall on U.N. International Day of Solidarity and called on Ireland to ban trade from Israeli settlements.

Cork has even passed a "twinning" mechanism with the Palestinian city of Nablus — a largely symbolic partnership.

IRISH PM REJECTS ANTISEMITISM CONCERNS IN IRELAND AMID DRAMATIC VOTE OVER BOYCOTTING ISRAEL GAME.

It has been revealed that conoe Kelliher from Ballyvourney holds a Palestinian flag whilst attending a watch-along party in the town square of Ireland's Eurovision entrant Bambie Thug's hometown of Macroom in Co Cork, as the Eurovision final takes place at Malmo Arena on Saturday, May 11, 2024. (Noel Sweeney/PA Images via Getty Images).

Fergal Dennehy, the lord mayor of Cork from 2025 to 2026, hosted the mayor of Nablus in February, calling the partnership "just the beginning of what we hope will be a wonderful relationship between our two great cities.".

Neither CPSC nor Cork City Council responded to Fox News Digital's requests for comment on the city's pro-Palestinian positions or about connections to O’Corráin.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that britt has made fighting elder financial abuse a priority.
  • Katie Britt on Wednesday aims to combat a rising diversity of financial fraud by unifying the U.S.
  • Recent findings suggest that the draft bill would establish a National Office for Scam and Fraud Prevention in the White House that would coordinate federal, state and private sector efforts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that britt has made fighting elder financial abuse a priority. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

A bill introduced by Sen. Katie Britt on Wednesday aims to combat a rising diversity of financial fraud by unifying the U.S. effort to fight it.

Recent findings suggest that the draft bill would establish a National Office for Scam and Fraud Prevention in the White House that would coordinate federal, state and private sector efforts. It is aimed at ensuring that federal agencies, law enforcement, financial institutions, telecommunications and technology companies and other groups work together, according to an overview from Britt.

The new office would promote intelligence sharing across the public and private sectors, coordinate consumer education efforts and improve assistance for victims.

Britt, R-Ala., noted the effort is needed because fraudsters operate nimbly utilizing social media while taking advantage of fragmented or disorganized responses from individual companies and government agencies.

In a recent development, “This effort is about bringing everyone to the table and making sure our response keeps pace with the criminals who are exploiting latest technologies and gaps between sectors,” she remarked in a statement. “When we work together to identify threats earlier and share information more effectively, we can better protect American families and businesses.”.

The office would develop a “lexicon of fraud” so that terms for different kinds of scams are standardized between various federal law enforcement agencies to promote a “whole-of-government response,” a Britt aide mentioned.

Industry observers note that the office also would work to broaden the approach to combating fraud beyond just having financial institutions reimburse victims. It would tap telecommunications and technology companies to address fraud at its source, such as rip-offs that start as text messages, social media posts or online advertisements.

It has been revealed that britt has made fighting elder financial abuse a priority. She is the sponsor of a bill that would allow state, local and tribal law enforcement agencies to use federal grant funding to investigate financial fraud, particularly scams targeted at the elderly.

The measure highlights the prevalence of "pig butchering," a common technique where a predator cultivates a personal relationship with a victim over many months to extract the most cash.

According to recent reports, the House passed its version of the bill in September with overwhelming bipartisan support. The House sponsor is Rep. Zach Nunn, R-Iowa.

Senior financial abuse also was the focus of a bill the House passed in an overwhelming 414-2 vote in June. The legislation, sponsored by Rep. Ann Wagner, R-Mo., would codify Securities and Exchange Commission guidance that permits mutual funds and their agents to postpone the sale of securities if there is a reasonable belief that financial exploitation of someone who is elderly or disabled is occurring.

It's not clear whether the Senate will take action on these bills or Britt's by the end of the year.

“If it doesn’t get through in the lame duck, it will continue to be a priority in the 120th [Congress],” the Britt aide mentioned.

It has been revealed that as luxury Amazon trips grow in popularity, operators are having to go further to deliver what they sell: remoteness. Gateway cities, including Brazil’s Manaus, are sprawling, and lodges that once felt remote no longer are.

As luxury Amazon trips grow in popularity, tourism is adding pressure to the very thing it’s sold on: remote, authentic experiences.

Tour operators increasingly define luxury as access to remote locations and unique experiences. As the industry grows, the gateways to these experiences, and especially to the Amazon in Brazil, are becoming more urbanized — threatening the very thing travelers are there to experience.

According to recent reports, one notable pressure point is waterways. CroisiEurope will debut luxury cruises from Brazil to Colombia next year, and Carnival Corporation’s Seabourn announced a latest cruise featuring Amazon river sailing for 2028. Lindblad also chartered a 42-guest ship to expand its presence in the Amazon for this year, doubling its capacity, and Ponant bought a majority stake in Aqua Expeditions, which runs Peruvian river cruises.

Amazonastur, the tourism agency in Brazil’s Amazonas state, expects to see 17,000 visitors including crew.

Former Southern Poverty Law Center executive Heidi Beirich faces federal charges of wire fraud and money laundering conspiracy. The Department of Justice alleges Beirich hid over $4 million in payments from SPLC donors to fund White supremacy.

A former Southern Poverty Law Center official who led its hate-group tracking work told FBI agents he tried to make the watchdog’s controversial "Hate Map" more ideologically balanced, while saying Christians and conservatives were the first staffers pushed out in what he called a "long-term coup" at the organization after he left in 2013.

According to recent reports, the former director stated he pushed for a more evenhanded SPLC, arguing that its "Hate Map" — which lists conservative groups alongside Ku Klux Klan chapters — should also include left-wing extremists, including violent animal-rights and extremist environmental groups. However, the former director said the effort met resistance and that, as liberal leaders reshaped the organization, most of his 17-person team was replaced.

"There was some kind of coup, long-term coup going on there between some, what I would — what I heard were some pretty liberal people, extreme people that had other ideas about what we were doing," the unnamed former director told agents, as first reported by The Daily Signal's Tyler O'Neil, who has been covering the SPLC's legal troubles.

DOJ EXPANDS INDICTMENT AGAINST SPLC, ALLEGING $4M SECRETLY FUNNELED TO KKK AND EXTREMIST GROUPS.

It has been revealed that SPLC Intelligence Project Director Heidi Beirich speaks during an event on Jan. 12, 2018. (David Buchan/Variety/Penske Media via Getty Images).

According to recent reports, the former director’s comments appeared in an FBI interview transcript filed as an exhibit to Dr. Heidi Beirich’s Nov. 2 court filing. Beirich, a former SPLC official charged alongside the organization in a federal case alleging a scheme to mislead donors and banks about donations used to pay informants associated with violent extremist groups, pointed to multiple FBI interviews with an unnamed former SPLC director, identified in the filing as "Individual-1.".

Sources indicate that in a January interview, Individual-1 told investigators he ran the SPLC’s field-source program, set up accounts used to pay sources and directed payments, according to Beirich’s filing. During a March 23 follow-up interview with Individual-1, FBI Special Agents David McDaniel and Parker Still framed the conversation around the program having "gone off the rails" under Beirich and told the former director they were not there to discuss the bank activity, noting he had "obviously nothing to do with all that," before questioning him about the SPLC’s alleged targeting of conservative organizations and Beirich’s role, according to the transcript.

EXCLUSIVE: SPLC'S 'FAR-LEFT,' 'ANTI-RACISM' CURRICULUM FOUND IN CLASSROOMS AS EARLY AS KINDERGARTEN: 'WATCHDOG'.

Individual-1 responded that, as his "gut impression," he believed her actions were political and accused some liberals at the center of having "a good degree of hatred" for conservatism, according to the March 23 transcript.

Individual-1 also alleged a shift in power at the SPLC. After he left in 2013, he mentioned, people were appointed to the SPLC’s board as "figureheads" and eventually gained enough voting power to take over the center. He said only one or two data-entry members of his roughly 17-person team remained, with the others replaced by staff he believed shared the new leadership’s politics.

"That's who they ran off first were the Christians and conservatives," the unnamed former director told agents when asked why Beirich took the actions she did after his departure. "Then they — then the rest they just replaced with people they liked, you know, that agreed with them politically.".

HOW MUTINY AT SOUTHERN POVERTY LAW CENTER TRIGGERED LEADERSHIP COLLAPSE.

The Southern Poverty Law Center (SPLC) building seen in March 2020 in Montgomery, Alabama. (Barry Lewis/InPictures via Getty Images).

In separate comments about the SPLC's controversial "Hate Map," Individual-1 said he persuaded SPLC staff, despite internal resistance, to list Black separatist groups, which he considered comparable to White racist groups, on the map. However, he said he unsuccessfully pushed the SPLC to include violent animal-rights and environmental extremist groups and described his team’s approach during his tenure as director as "very nonpartisan" and "middle of the road.".

"We were very nonpartisan, or at least when I was running things, when I was director, we stayed right in the middle of the road," he noted.

In a June follow-up, the unnamed former director also criticized the SPLC's "Hate Map" for listing local chapters separately, saying it made the map's totals of the extremist groups it chose to identify look larger.

WATCH: SPLC CHIEF DOUBLES DOWN ON PLACING CHARLIE KIRK'S TURNING POINT USA ON 'HATE MAP'.

Industry observers note that while the unnamed former director was not charged in the SPLC case, Beirich was. Her lawyers say the interviews with the unnamed director warrant discovery into whether she was singled out because of her perceived role in the SPLC’s political speech, arguing that investigators’ questions about the SPLC’s treatment of conservative groups — and her alleged role in that work — could show the prosecution was motivated by hostility to the center’s political speech.

"Individual-1’s statements confirm my longstanding criticism of the Southern Poverty Law Center, that it exaggerates ‘hate’ by inflating the chapters on its ‘hate map’ and that it systematically demonizes conservatives and Christians while turning a blind eye to extremism on the Left," O’Neil, the author of "Making Hate Pay: The Corruption of the Southern Poverty Law Center," told Fox News Digital. "Now, we have the former director of the Intelligence Project saying the SPLC appears to have pushed out Christians and conservatives, while rejecting his suggestion to include environmentalist agitators on the map.".

Fox News Digital reached out to the SPLC and attorneys for Heidi Beirich for comment but did not receive a response in time for publication.

Sources indicate that A common framework makes it easier for operators to benchmark against one another and their suppliers, but the burden still falls on operators to collect and crunch the numbers. The best way to get tour operators to calculate their emissions would be releasing a tool to do it for them.

In 2026, hotels tend to report emissions on a per-room basis, trains report per passenger, and a bus company reports its emissions for the whole vehicle. From these fragmented data points, a package tour operator has to fold all of those numbers into one to understand its climate impact.

Two tour operator associations have developed a website they hope can help solve this problem. The idea is to simplify emissions calculations for package tour operators by bringing resources into one place.

Industry observers note that the site, called TEMPO, is the work of the European Tourism Association (ETOA) and United States Tour Operators Association (USTOA). It points to free methodologies operators can use to measure emissions and to free calculation tools for each part of a tour, as well as identifying when one doesn’t exist.

“A tour operator has to piece together data from many suppliers, each measuring a different service in a different unit,” ETOA’s director gene.

Breaking: Democrats nominate Jeffries to be House speaker, a historic first

💡 Key Takeaways
  • House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., flanked by House Minority Whip Katherine M.
  • House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries won a closed-door vote of the Democratic caucus Wednesday setting him up to be the nation’s first Black speaker of the House, a historic step that follows Democrats’ staggering election wins earlier this month.
  • Jeffries, who had called for a recorded vote of the more than 250-member caucus that will serve in the next Congress despite facing no revealed opponent, won decisively, 251-11.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., flanked by House Minority Whip Katherine M. Clark, D-Mass., and House Democratic Caucus Chair Pete Aguilar, D-Calif., hold a press conference in the Capitol after the House Democratic leadership elections on Wednesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries won a closed-door vote of the Democratic caucus Wednesday setting him up to be the nation’s first Black speaker of the House, a historic step that follows Democrats’ staggering election wins earlier this month.

Jeffries, who had called for a recorded vote of the more than 250-member caucus that will serve in the next Congress despite facing no revealed opponent, won decisively, 251-11. The margin suggests Jeffries will easily surpass the necessary 218 votes he will need on the House floor when the full chamber votes in January.

“It's a high honor and a distinct privilege to stand before the American people today as a Democratic nominee to be the next Speaker of the United States House of Representatives,” Jeffries said at a press conference following the election.

Industry observers note that while Jeffries celebrates his win, he has continued to put an emphasis on unity before he faces what has been deemed the toughest job in Washington. Democrats’ massive majority will give him some margin for maneuvering as he balances the priorities of a complex caucus ranging from moderates to progressives.

“Our job is to fight MAGA extremism, not each other,” Jeffries responded when asked about the 11 defections and what they mean for the next Congress. “Fight MAGA extremism, and to get significant things done for the American people, and that is what we are going to accomplish together, beginning on January 3rd.”.

Seven of the 11 members who intended to vote against Jeffries released a statement saying that conversations with leadership are still “ongoing” and that there is “work to be done,” but noting there has been “meaningful progress.” The seven included Reps.- elect Darializa Avilia Chavelier, D-N.Y., Adam Hamawy, D-N.J., Frederick Haynes, D-Texas, Melat Kiros, D-Colo., Donovan McKinney, D-Mich., Chris Rabb, D-Pa., and Claire Valdez, D-N.Y.

“Whether on Medicare for All, stopping ICE terror, getting money out of politics, or ending the genocide in Gaza, our constituents sent us to Congress with a mandate on these issues,” they wrote. “We have worked to secure commitments from Leader Jeffries in good-faith conversations.”.

Newly elected House Democrats will meet with former President Barack Obama Wednesday night, where party unity will also be a likely topic.

Recent findings suggest that “This is the beginning of a new bargain, a new politics where hard work is honored and where people's voice is paramount, and where we have more confidence in the future than nostalgia for the past,” House Minority Whip Katherine M. Clark, D-Mass., noted at the press conference.

Rep. Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., who made history two decades ago as the nation’s first female speaker, arrived for the vote chanting “Hakeem Jeffries!”, reflecting party leaders’ desire to start the long morning of balloting on a positive note.

According to recent reports, jeffries' nomination followed the election of current Democratic Caucus Vice Chairman Ted Lieu, D-Calif., to serve as the caucus chair in the next Congress. Separate votes followed Wednesday morning, keeping Jeffries' leadership team intact: Clark, as the fresh majority leader and Democratic Caucus Chairman Pete Aguilar, D-Calif., as majority whip.

At his news conference, Jeffries noted that Clark was also making history as the first woman ever to serve in the position. Aguilar will also be the first Latino to serve as majority whip.

“We've been looking at people's talents, not a particular gender or race, and I think that's a good thing,” outgoing Rep. Steny H. Hoyer, D-Md., a former majority leader, told reporters ahead of the election.

According to recent reports, “I think Hakeem Jeffries is going to be a good speaker,” Hoyer continued. “He has the confidence of the caucus, and he has a good leadership team that is close knit and very organized.”.

Jeffries expressed confidence in the weeks leading up to his securing the top Democratic spot in the House, brushing aside questions about incoming members who had mentioned they remained “undecided” ahead of the election.

Industry observers note that pelosi was nominated for speaker by acclamation ahead of her first election to the position in 2007. But Jeffries’ allies portrayed his decision to move forward with a recorded vote as a show of strength after a group of incoming progressives had floated forcing a recorded vote in the internal leadership race.

Sources indicate that the entire leadership team will be tested despite their numerical advantage over Republicans by the same internal tensions facing Senate Democrats, where current Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., is being challenged for leadership of the majority by Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md.

Jeffries mentioned Tuesday that the approach to the caucus vote mirrored the caucus’ 2018 transition from minority to majority, giving members an opportunity to weigh in on who was best positioned to lead based on their “track record, experience and vision.”.

Jeffries has already outlined some of his top priorities of his speakership such as a hefty healthcare agenda, immigration legislation, and a multitude of investigations into the Trump administration.

He also signaled Wednesday another area where his party’s restive base is likely to close ranks: oversight.

“House Democrats will hold the crooks accountable, not for partisan reasons, but for patriotic ones,” he remarked at his news conference.

  • Some Senate Democrats have heartburn about President Donald Trump’s planned Thursday meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping, but Republicans counter by saying he could get the Russian and Chinese leaders to budge on a list of problems even as he appears politically weakened at home.
  • Trump arrived Wednesday in China’s Shenzhen economic zone on the banks of the Pearl River ahead of a high-level summit that was ostensibly slated to focus on paring each countries’ nuclear arsenal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that president Donald Trump prepares to shake hands with Russian President Vladimir Putin as China's President Xi Jinping looks on before the welcome banquet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. (Iori Sagisawa / POOL / AFP via Getty Images).

Some Senate Democrats have heartburn about President Donald Trump’s planned Thursday meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping, but Republicans counter by saying he could get the Russian and Chinese leaders to budge on a list of problems even as he appears politically weakened at home.

Trump arrived Wednesday in China’s Shenzhen economic zone on the banks of the Pearl River ahead of a high-level summit that was ostensibly slated to focus on paring each countries’ nuclear arsenal. But before he left, Trump signaled the three-way talks also likely would include the artificial intelligence race, Moscow’s bloody war with Ukraine, global trade and his standoff with Iran.

The U.S. commander in chief’s tendency to sound deferential to Putin and habit of referring to Xi as a personal “friend” concerns many congressional Democrats. But Trump’s GOP allies on Capitol Hill, despite this month’s midterm election losses, still describe him as a dealmaker who has a chance to use his final years to bend Putin and Xi toward U.S. interests.

Rick Scott, a Florida Republican who sits on the Senate Armed Services and Foreign Relations committees, said Tuesday he was hopeful that Trump could make some progress on at least one matter with the Russian and Chinese leaders.

Recent findings suggest that “As we all know, China and Russia want to destroy our way of life,” he remarked. “But it would be great to reduce … nuclear stockpiles and make sure we're not going to ever get attacked.

Sources indicate that still, Scott sounded skeptical about two world leaders Trump has tried to keep close during his two terms. “But do I trust Xi or Putin? No, they're a bunch of liars.” Asked if he worries Trump might trust them too much, Scott replied: “I don't think he trusts him any more than I do. … I'm glad the president's trying. Hope springs eternal. But do I actually really believe something good's going to come out of it? I don't.”.

Outgoing House Armed Services Vice Chair Rob Wittman, R-Va., noted part of Trump’s talks on Thursday “should be to make sure the world is a safer place, to make sure we don't have aggressive behavior like Russia in an unprovoked attack against Ukraine.

“They ought to be talking about how they don't do those sorts of things, how they don't threaten their neighbors, how they don't try to intimidate through the assertion of force that they ought to be able to work together to make sure we assure a safe globe,” stated Wittman, who lost his reelection race earlier this month.

That comment came one day after Trump told reporters as he left the White House for Asia that he sees Putin “backing down a little bit” in his conduct of the war with Ukraine.

“I think he could be tougher. I think he could be a lot tougher, frankly,” Trump said Monday. “I think he's backing down.”.

Those kinds of deferential remarks about the Russian leader are a major reason why some Democrats have heartburn about Thursday’s meeting.

Sources indicate that senate Armed Services member Mazie K. Hirono, D-Hawaii, stated Tuesday that she’s concerned about the Shenzhen summit because “I’m not sure what’s going to pop out of [Trump’s] mouth next — especially for a meeting with two guys he clearly likes.”.

According to recent reports, sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., also a member of the Armed Services and Foreign Relations committees, stated he has “high hopes” for the trilateral meeting — but “maybe not high expectations.”.

“I have some points of anxiety. I'm nervous about any discussion about Ukraine that doesn't involve the Ukrainians. And, so, some of the advance to this is like, ‘We're going to talk about ending the Ukraine war.’ You can't do that without Ukraine at the table,” Kaine stated. “So the desire to bring about more peace and stability, that's a good thing to talk about. But no conditions about Ukraine and ending that war without them at the table? Not so sure about that.”.

It has been revealed that during remarks Tuesday on the Senate floor, Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer criticized what he described as Trump’s misplaced priorities.

According to recent reports, “Enforcement of the new rules restricting China’s access to our most sensitive AI chips should start today,” the New York Democrat stated, adding that Trump should focus more of his Asia swing on securing commitments from U.S. allies to block China from gaining an upper hand in the AI technology race.

Trump touted just that on Tuesday during remarks in Manila at a U.S.-Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit in the Philippines.

“Since I returned to office, we've made major trade deals with Malaysia, Cambodia, Indonesia, as well as Japan, South Korea, and almost everybody, frankly, at the table,” he noted. “And we've made many other vital agreements across the region spanning energy, critical minerals and technology.”.

But on Wednesday, Trump appeared to have pivoted to the trip’s main event.

He stood beside Xi at an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen and smiled as Putin approached. Trump extended his hand and shook Putin’s as the Chinese leader looked on.

Scott, a Trump ally in the Senate, stated Tuesday he sees the president “trying to build relationships to try to make sure we don't end up at war [because] he doesn't like war.”.

It has been revealed that trump signaled Monday that he might press Xi for details on an alleged Chinese spy who had an affair with Nvidia founder Jensen Huang, costing the AI mogul his job as the company’s president and CEO. He also said he could bring up Nvidia’s sales of sophisticated microchips that many lawmakers — Republican and Democrat — want to ensure remain in the U.S. for domestic AI development.

Sources indicate that the administration’s response to the turmoil at Nvidia, with Trump even suggesting he'd support Huang returning as CEO, is a rare area where Republicans have expressed concern publicly. House Energy and Commerce Committee Chair Brett Guthrie, R-Kent., wrote to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Wednesday seeking information about “the implementation of federal laws governing technology exports, in particular the application of export controls relating to semiconductor chips, the effect of which has a broad impact on America’s race with China to artificial intelligence (AI) dominance and the ability of U.S. companies to set global technology standards.”.

Heather Williams, director of the Project on Nuclear Complications at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, wrote this week that for the three leaders, the “path is fraught with challenges.”.

In a recent development, “Putin could diplomatically outmaneuver the Trump administration and make any progress on nuclear complications dependent on undermining Western support to Ukraine,” she wrote in an analysis for the Washington, D.C.-based think tank. “Even the optics of Trump and Putin negotiating while the war continues and as Russia ramps up missile strikes on Ukrainian civilian targets could be interpreted as undermining U.S. values.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that travelers are moving from talking about getting outside to booking experiences that take them there. Newly introduced research from Boatsetter points to growing participation in outdoor and water-based activities, creating opportunities for hospitality brands to make shared experiences more accessible.

This sponsored content was created in collaboration with a Skift partner.

According to recent reports, people have spent years saying they want to spend less time on their screens. Now more of them are acting on it. Boatsetter, a booking platform for boat sharing and on-water experiences, tracks that shift in its newly introduced report, Great Outdoor Shift 2.0. The report draws on two online surveys of U.S. adults: 834 in December 2025 and 1,034 in September 2026.

Boatsetter’s 2026 Great Outdoor Shift survey indicates people responding to digital overload: 77% of respondents said they had already reduced screen time and social media use, and 63% said they would trade screen time for time on or near the water. The pull is about well-being, too: 84% say the outdoors is important for their mental health.

According to recent reports, “People aren’t just tired of their screens. They want something that makes them feel small and present. That’s what awe does, and it’s why time on the water with friends keeps topping the list of what Americans want most,” said Michael Farb, CEO of Boatsetter.

It has been revealed that comparing the two surveys, Boatsetter reports a 64% increase in the number of people who tried fishing or paddlesports, a sign that participation is growing. Research from Tripadvisor supports this: In the first half of 2026, U.S. bookings on Tripadvisor grew 57% for fishing charters and 37% for boat rentals compared with the same period in 2025, according to the company’s 2026 Mid-Year Experiences Trends Report.

For hotels, destinations, and other travel providers, the figures point to demand for experiences that bring people into a destination, not just around it.

Recent findings suggest that boatsetter’s research also points to a broader shift toward active, social travel. Time on the water with friends remains the experience respondents most want more of. Spending intent is rising, too: 82% plan to spend more on outdoor or water activities in 2027, and 37.5% of this year’s respondents want to spend significantly more, compared with 23.4% in Boatsetter’s 2025 survey. For hospitality brands, the practical opportunity lies in helping guests discover and book experiences, from guided excursions to activities with local operators.

Sources indicate that the pull toward the outdoors extends beyond water activities. Hilton’s 2026 Trends Report, based on a survey of 14,009 adults in 13 countries who plan to travel in the next 12 months, found that rest and recharging is the top motivation for leisure travel, cited by 56% of respondents. Spending time in nature was also among their top desires, with 37% citing it as such. Both findings point to demand for experiences that help travelers step away from routine.

Great Outdoor Shift 2.0 explores three questions for travel and hospitality leaders:.

Recent findings suggest that taken together, the findings point to a role for travel companies that goes beyond providing a view of nature. In 2027, hotels, tourism boards, and travel partners can make shared outdoor activities easier to access through local partnerships, clearer booking options, and experiences suited to different interests. The opportunity is to help guests follow through on the time they already say they want outdoors.

“We’ve known the desire to get outside is there. What’s changing is that people are acting on it, and they expect technology to help, not get in the way. Our job is to make the outdoor experiences they want easy to reach,” Farb remarked.

The rejections of Viktor Orbán and Donald Trump hold sobering lessons for the nationalist right.

On Election Night this past May in Budapest, I was in the ballroom when a defining political era ended faster than it takes to place a drink order at a party-district ruin bar on a Saturday night. Viktor Orbán, the four-term prime minister who for 16 years was the undisputed sovereign of Hungarian politics, and the monster that haunted the nightmares of globalists from Brussels to Washington, took the stage not long after election results began rolling in — and gracefully accepted defeat. It was as if magician David Copperfield had made the Matterhorn disappear before the audience settled into its chairs on the chalet lawn.

Sources indicate that just like that, Orbán was gone. When I first arrived in Budapest for a fellowship in 2021, a Hungarian conservative friend told me that everybody knows Orbán’s Fidesz Party is riddled with corruption, but people tolerate it because life has been getting better and better for them since the reformist prime minister took power in 2010. “But if the economy ever turns,” he remarked, “then corruption is going to matter. A lot.”.

Rod Dreher is the author of six books, including the Fresh York Times bestsellers The Benedict Option (2017) and Live Not By Lies (2020).

A dozen cities in Los Angeles and Orange counties raised or updated lodging taxes in recent elections as cities prepare for a surge in visitors during the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

Five months after Los Angeles voters rejected an increase to the city’s lodging tax, the surrounding suburbs hiked their own.

Recent findings suggest that preliminary results show 12 cities in Los Angeles and Orange counties approving changes to lodging taxes on November 3, according to the California Local Government Finance Almanac. Ten created or raised rates, with two cities pushing their hotel rates above Los Angeles’ 14% tax. Two expanded their current tax to cover more types of stays.

Industry observers note that the changes come as Los Angeles and the surrounding area prepare for a surge in visitation for the 2028 Olympics, which are expected to draw in roughly 2 million visitors to the greater Los Angeles area, and as local lawmakers work to address widening budget gaps. Skift previously reported that lodging taxes can be an easy sell because the people paying them aren’t usually locals who vote.

FCC pick advanced by Senate Commerce after Democratic boycott

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (891 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ted Cruz, R-Texas, talks with reporters after the Senate luncheons in the Capitol on Tuesday.
  • The fight over partisan balance on the Federal Communications Commission snarled a Senate markup Wednesday morning as Republicans advanced a controversial nomination despite a Democratic boycott in an attempt to deny a quorum.
  • Republicans on the Commerce Committee voted unanimously to advance the nomination of Danielle Thumann Severs, a senior counsel to FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, to be a member of the commission, alongside several transportation and communications bills.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, talks with reporters after the Senate luncheons in the Capitol on Tuesday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

The fight over partisan balance on the Federal Communications Commission snarled a Senate markup Wednesday morning as Republicans advanced a controversial nomination despite a Democratic boycott in an attempt to deny a quorum.

Republicans on the Commerce Committee voted unanimously to advance the nomination of Danielle Thumann Severs, a senior counsel to FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, to be a member of the commission, alongside several transportation and communications bills.

The fate of the nominations and bills could ultimately be decided via a challenge on the Senate floor, according to a Democratic committee staffer, speaking on condition of anonymity.

In a statement Wednesday morning, committee Democrats, led by ranking member  Maria Cantwell of Washington, mentioned they objected to Thumann Severs’ nomination without a Democratic “pair” nomination and referenced a letter they sent to Chairman Ted Cruz, R-Texas, on Monday requesting the nomination be removed from the agenda.

“Commissioner Anna Gomez could be re-nominated with all swiftness, as we have called for numerous times,” the group wrote. “This is not a problem we created, but a problem that the White House can solve.”.

Thumann Severs, if confirmed, would give the FCC three Republican members and one Democrat, Gomez. The three Republicans could then constitute a quorum on the commission, allowing President Donald Trump to potentially fire Gomez. The commission generally has five members, three of the president’s party and two in the minority.

Cruz said at the markup that there is nothing in the law that requires moving nominees in pairs, and that committee Republicans would continue their work on what he called a nomination that followed a “typical process.”.

“Democrats will control the Senate, unfortunately, in January,” Cruz said. “But today is November 18th. The American people elected each of us to fulfill our duties, including advice and consent, for our full terms.”.

Related: Threats to broadcasters hang over FCC nominee hearing.

The Democratic staffer told reporters that because the committee did not adopt rules at the beginning of the 119th Congress, it has been operating under rules from the 118th, which required the attendance of at least one member of the minority party to constitute a quorum for reporting bills or nominations.

According to recent reports, “The remaining recourse is to basically go to the floor and . . . make an inquiry in terms of what took place today, and then there would have to be a formal ruling by the chair,” they said.

They added that in determining whether the committee had a quorum to advance the nomination, “It would depend on how they view our committee rules from the 118th that we practice under for the 119th versus what the Senate rules are.” The staffer said they have not yet spoken with committee Democrats or Democratic leadership about intends for such an inquiry.

Democrats also previously boycotted a committee markup in March over an aviation safety bill left off the committee’s agenda, after which action was deferred. The committee later came to agreement and rescheduled the markup.

In their letter Monday, Democrats quoted Cruz from a 2014 statement about the nomination of Loretta Lynch to be attorney general.

“As you wrote in 2014, controversial nominees ‘should not be confirmed in the lame duck session of Congress by senators who just lost their seats and are no longer accountable to the voters.’ We agree,” the letter mentioned.

On Tuesday, Sen. Ben Ray Luján, D-N.M., wrote his own letter to Cruz calling for the removal of the nomination from the agenda based on grounds that Thumann Severs lied to the committee.

According to recent reports, “While Ms. Thumann testified she did not work ‘on any media-related complications,’ documents obtained through Freedom of Information Act requests demonstrate that she worked on several media related issues, including on commitments that Skydance made to pave the way for FCC approval of its merger with Paramount,” Luján wrote.

Democrats have criticized the FCC and Carr for allowing media consolidation, including by Skydance. There has also been bipartisan criticism of Carr’s threats against broadcasters for speech he disagrees with.

Luján told reporters Wednesday prior to the markup that he expects, under Democratic control next year, Carr and potentially Thumann Severs would be called to testify.

It has been revealed that “I have questions. I certainly hope that Brendan Carr will voluntarily show up to this committee when invited, and that other rules and tools do not need to be used,” Luján stated, responding to a question about possibly subpoenaing Carr. “But . . . everything should be on the table.”.

Sen. Jerry Moran, R-Kan., stated at the markup that he spoke with Thumann Severs about her role at the FCC and her “lack of engagement” as the commission has made decisions regarding broadcasters. He also said he found her testimony at last week’s nomination hearing “comforting.”.

“I have concerns with FCC action in regard to political speech, broadcasters, and she indicated in her answers . . . in a way that provided me with a level of comfort about her nomination in regard to that issue,” Moran said.

Moran also said he hopes to meet with Thumann Severs before her nomination is brought to the floor.

Industry observers note that riyadh’s hotels lost their peak season when the airport shut. With BA, Cathay Pacific and others suspended into the new year and Houthi strikes still hitting the capital, the recovery hasn’t started.

Industry observers note that riyadh hotels had one of their worst months of the year in October. A temporary shutdown of the city’s main airport cut off inbound demand just as peak season started.

It has been revealed that occupancy fell 34.7 percentage points year over year to 34.3% from 69%, according to CoStar’s STR. Only March had lower occupancy, at 28.3%. Average daily rate dropped 29.9% to $190 and revenue per available room (RevPAR) fell 65.1% to $65.

“October and November are usually the peak season months for Riyadh, so the impact is much bigger,” said Kostas Nikolaidis, associate account director for Middle East and Africa at STR.

Industry observers note that the October demand collapse traces back to an attack on King Khalid International Airport. The airport closed after an attack on Oct. 10 that Saudi authorities said killed 13 people and injured more than 300. Some 86% of scheduled Riyadh departures were canceled between Oct. 8 and late October, according to Cirium data, Skift repor.

In the first year, the the age of Medicare eligibility would drop to 55 from 65, while coverage would expand to include dental, hearing and vision care. The age of eligibility would fall another 10 years in each of the following years until the fourth year, when coverage would be extended to all Americans.

#6812. Can Rocky Save the World?

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (796 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nationalreview ↗ Open Full Page

Can Rocky Save the World?

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (796 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nationalreview

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sylvester Stallone has been a Hollywood institution for so long — his breakthrough movie Rocky premiered 50 years ago — that his previous underdog status as a struggling actor seems perfectly mythic in the latest behind-the-scenes biographical drama I Play Rocky.
  • Industry observers note that the fairy-tale aspect of I Play Rocky comes from its background story.
  • According to recent reports, starting with Stallone practicing elocution (using Walt Whitman’s “I Sing the Body Electric”) to soften his rough Latest York accent, the film then places him against odds in an era of cultural ferment that included such films as Altman’s The Long Goodbye and Coppola’s The Conversation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sylvester Stallone has been a Hollywood institution for so long — his breakthrough movie Rocky premiered 50 years ago — that his previous underdog status as a struggling actor seems perfectly mythic in the latest behind-the-scenes biographical drama I Play Rocky.

Industry observers note that the fairy-tale aspect of I Play Rocky comes from its background story. In this, young Stallone (played by Anthony Ippolito) is a virtually homeless outsider, working at a movie theater, who after spending 16 months on writing eight screenplays, joins the creative zeitgeist of 1970s Hollywood, also known as the American Renaissance. It is this personal journey that illuminates the Stallone legend that climaxes with Rocky winning the Academy Award for best picture over such esteemed movies as Taxi Driver, Network, Bound for Glory, and All the President’s Men.

According to recent reports, starting with Stallone practicing elocution (using Walt Whitman’s “I Sing the Body Electric”) to soften his rough Latest York accent, the film then places him against odds in an era of cultural ferment that included such films as Altman’s The Long Goodbye and Coppola’s The Conversation. (Stallone pays particular attention to the intonation of Coppola’s actors repeating the line “He’d kill us if he found out.”) Screenwriter Peter Gamble doesn’t make that detail ominous but simplifies the life-or-death aspect of Stallone’s career and artistic ambition as part of the wannabe actor’s desperate, working-class consciousness — inspired by viewing the heavyweight championship boxing match between Muhammad Ali and Chuck Wepner. It’s easier to take than the sociological theme in Green Book, the egregious previous film of director Peter Farrelly. I Play Rocky regains the genial humanism of such Farrelly brothers’ movies as Me, Myself and Irene, Stuck on You, and The Ringer, and especially the Farrelly brothers’ script for Outside Providence.

Kiki Seto (Talia Shire) and Anthony Ippolito (Sylvester Stallone) in I Play Rocky.

Stallone’s ambition is epitomized by his insistence that the Rocky screenplay he wrote in four days and sold to producers Irwin Winkler and Robert Chartoff can be filmed only starring himself. He demands, “I play Rocky.” That’s not a playground taunt in the milieu of financial bargaining and egotism that’s gleefully depicted by a series of Hollywood types — P. J. Byrne and Toby Kebbell as Winkler and Chartoff, Rob Demery as Joe Frazier, and a standout cameo by Trevor St. John as a self-serious fight coordinator.

In a recent development, in Hollywood’s gladiatorial circus, Stallone’s striving and eventual success become a credible moral victory. He must claim his own identity and career path separately from his worldly father Frank (Matt Dillon gives a moving characterization of a parent’s cynicism, affection, and personal regret). His wife Sasha (AnnaSophie Robb) encourages him: “I’d rather be optimistic and be wrong than pessimistic and be right.” These backstage details (including a hostile producer who dismisses Stallone as “a droopy-eyed hack actor”) make I Play Rocky a credible and appealing saga of Stallone’s indefatigable confidence. The movie rejects the sort of dark, objectionable narcissism that we saw in the Springsteen hagiography Deliver Me from Nowhere.

According to recent reports, it is important that the filmmakers accurately measure Rocky’s significance. Farrelly and Gamble mix film history with good sense and humor when portraying wild-eyed director John Avildsen (Jay Duplass) deep in his own world of pragmatic professionalism (“Great art never comes through compromise”). They also capture Stallone’s own, uncanny sense of achieving the proper effect — not so much when Rocky emotes to his manager Mickey as when, in a startling shot, he points to details in a big-screen image of Kirk Douglas in Champion, from 1948.

In a recent development, putting Rocky in proper perspective is a curatorial feat. It recognizes Stallone’s film as a work of pop lore. Its popularity gave Hollywood the opportunity to ignore scary powerful art like Scorsese’s Taxi Driver in favor of the folk and commercial elements that are easily enjoyed in American culture — although missing from Millennial film culture. Remember: In 1976, Rocky seemed an artificial retread of old boxing films, pilfering the ethnic sentimentality of Marty, On the Waterfront, and Requiem for a Heavyweight as if Muhammad Ali had never happened.

According to recent reports, but I Play Rocky works differently. It recalls Stallone’s response to Wepner (“This guy won’t go down!”) to achieve the authentic Millennial pop lore of Better Man, Song Sung Blue, Back 2 America, Power Ballad, and the upcoming Madden. (These restorative myths correct the disappointing Creed sequels that failed to live up to Rocky.) I Play Rocky channels Stallone’s personal perseverance to enlighten our current demoralized sensibilities.

Armond White is National Review’s culture critic and the author of New Position: The Prince Chronicles and Make Spielberg Great Again: The Steven Spielberg Chronicles.

Industry News: Restored to Calder’s plan, the clouds are spinning again

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Alex Padilla, D-Calif., speaks during a ceremony marking the restoration of Alexander Calder’s Mountains and Clouds sculpture in the Hart Senate Office Building atrium on Wednesday.
  • The day after Alexander Calder presented his initiative for a public art display in the Hart Building’s nine-story atrium to the Architect of the Capitol, he died.
  • Rower felt a sense of awe as he stared up at his grandfather’s work, finally restored to what he had envisioned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sen. Alex Padilla, D-Calif., speaks during a ceremony marking the restoration of Alexander Calder’s Mountains and Clouds sculpture in the Hart Senate Office Building atrium on Wednesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

The day after Alexander Calder presented his initiative for a public art display in the Hart Building’s nine-story atrium to the Architect of the Capitol, he died.

Fifty years later, Alexander S.C. Rower felt a sense of awe as he stared up at his grandfather’s work, finally restored to what he had envisioned.

“It’s totally phenomenal,” he said, pointing up at the now-moving clouds as he spoke, spinning his finger around. “It’s not entertainment, but it’s trying to emulate naturalness, trying to emulate what nature would do.”.

It was a long time coming for Rower, who remembers traveling to the Capitol in his 20s for the original dedication of the Mountains and Clouds sculpture in 1987. The mobile portion stopped rotating as Calder intended in the 1990s, and it was ultimately removed in 2014 after being deemed unsafe by the Architect of the Capitol. Millions of dollars in private philanthropy later, Calder’s clouds are spinning again.

Industry observers note that rower was back on the Hill on Wednesday for an event celebrating the restoration, joining Architect of the Capitol Thomas Austin, Sens. Alex Padilla, D-Calif., Angus King, I-Maine, and James Lankford, R-Okla., and the project’s donors. As the speakers addressed the crowd, the clouds began to speed up slightly. Onlookers gathered on the balconies overlooking the atrium and peeked through office windows. Attendees left with tote bags emblazoned with images of Calder’s art.

According to Rower, who leads the Calder Foundation dedicated to preserving and interpreting his grandfather’s art, the mobile is rotating on a 15-hour cycle that is “totally variable.”.

Recent findings suggest that “It can go a little faster; it can go a little slower,” he remarked. “I told the team today that during lunchtime, I want it to speed up just a little bit because everyone’s going to lunch. There’ll be … a lot of activity passing through, and then right at 2:30, well, let’s make it go quieter.”.

It was a labor of love for those involved, and not an inexpensive one. Jon and Kim Shirley funded the $12 million restoration. Because the pieces were so large, they were transported on an extra-wide load truck and driven at a speed of 35 miles per hour from Michigan.

According to recent reports, “We had to call every senator or governor that we knew on that route, which went through seven states, to get permissions,” he stated. “That was a huge thing to overcome, and it all happened over a weekend. So my wife was actually on the phone with a governor’s wife on Saturday evening. The next day, he called up his Department of Transportation and got a permit.”.

Christian Quilici, who helped manage the project on behalf of the Shirleys and mentioned he serves as a liaison between the foundation and Congress, said the hardest part of the project was the size of it.

Industry observers note that “We had to tear the wall down on C Street, which nobody really thought of in the beginning,” he noted. “Nobody got how big this was until it showed up on their doorstep.”.

Quilici said he spent years educating at least 30 different senators about the quest to reunite the mobile with the stationary mountains left behind. Some of the biggest champions were seated in the front row at Wednesday’s event, including Senate Democratic Whip Richard J. Durbin. Absent was Sen. Christopher S. Murphy, D-Conn., who has been away from the Capitol while recovering from a stroke but has been a supporter of the sculpture’s restoration for years, pressing former acting Architect of the Capitol Joseph DiPietro on it at a 2024 Senate Legislative Branch Appropriations budget hearing.

“Is there any chance that before I leave the Senate, or at least before I die, we can get the clouds back up there?” Murphy said at the time.

Padilla read a letter on Wednesday from Murphy, whose state was Calder’s home for much of his life.

Sources indicate that “This statue is actually a statement on our democracy, that we have big pieces of monumental art right in the middle of our most key and most iconic government buildings. To get this piece of art restored to how it was designed by the artist, well, that’s good for Connecticut. But I also like to think … it’s good for democracy too,” Murphy’s statement said.

The restoration was funded entirely by donations from the Shirleys, who are prominent Calder collectors, according to Rower.

“It’s very emotional to see the work completed after 10 years of us working so hard with the Architect of the Capitol and Calder Foundation. It’s a very overpowering, overwhelming emotion,” stated Kim Shirley.

It has been revealed that in addition to helping fund the project, she’s a former Senate staffer who worked in Hart before Calder’s work was installed. Years after her time in the Senate was over, her husband Jon wanted to show her the sculpture, now filling the space she used to walk through every day.

But when the two arrived, the clouds weren’t hanging from the ceiling like they were supposed to be. He called up Rower, who was a friend of his, and remarked he wanted to get them back to how Calder intended. On Wednesday, the three of them stood together in Hart, looking up.

Technological and engineering advancements allowed for newer, lighter clouds to be built and be safe to hang from the ceiling.

“Before it was like a bulb, it looked like a hoagie sandwich, and now it looks just really sharp, like a razor cutting through space, which was Calder’s intention,” Rower noted.

According to Rower, it involved laser-measuring the original model of Mountains and Clouds sitting in a glass case nearby in the Hart atrium. The newly introduced clouds, he mentioned, are made of carbon fiber.

“These are giant things up in the air, and they’re just so gentle and subtle,” he said.

It has been revealed that younger Hill staffers don’t know a time with clouds. But for those who have spent decades in the building, it was a special moment to see them spin, as Lankford told the crowd.

“I can’t tell you how many tour groups that I’ve walked through this building and I pointed to this, and I said it’s only half there, and would take them over to the little model that’s right over here, and say this is what it’s supposed to look like,” said the senator, a former Hill staffer himself.

Standing under his grandfather’s sculpture, Rower found himself quoting the man responsible for it all.

“I find that everything I do, if it is made for a particular spot, is more successful,” he mentioned, gazing up at it.

It has been revealed that on the last day before the 2026 midterm elections, President Donald Trump gave a speech before the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, a site of considerable scandal in his second term. He joked it should be renamed after him and spent considerable time discussing Washington, D.C. construction projects and resurrecting conspiracy theories about monument vandals. When the president did turn to the elections, more than 23 minutes into an hour-long speech, he seemed to foreshadow major Republican losses in the House and Senate, describing it as “The most crucial midterm, I believe, in our lifetime.”.

“When you vote, remember a party that hates America cannot be allowed to rule over the people who built our country,” Trump stated, referring to Democrats, whom he said want to “blow all of this up by electing communist jihadists.”.

Sources indicate that “If the people that voted for me and voted in the last election where we had such a great victory, if they go out and vote, just a good portion of them, we will win in a landslide,” Trump mentioned midway in his speech. “Now that doesn’t happen because usually whoever the sitting president is, Republican or Democrat, uh, good or bad, good president, great president, bad, for some reason the sitting president doesn’t win the midterms, but we gave this a very strong shot.”.

The last day of polling indicates that Democrats have odds that are better than good to flip control of the House and Senate. The final results from the Upcoming York Times/Siena University polls report “The party is ahead in all seven states likeliest to decide control of the Senate: Michigan, Kansas, Texas, Maine, Ohio and, more narrowly, Alaska and Iowa.” The final predictions in the Cook Political Report included five additional shifts for Democrats in North Carolina, Florida, Tennessee and Virginia, projecting “that Democrats will win 15 to 25 seats, putting them at a 230- to 240-seat majority.” If a sweep happens in the toss up races, it’ll give Democrats their strongest majority since 2009.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, early voting records have been smashed around the country, in places like South Carolina and Ohio. In Texas, more than 7.7 million voters did so early, surpassing the record turnout for a midterm election set in 2018. Across the nation, about 50 million ballots have already been cast so far, with the share of registered Democrats notably increased in several key state races. But according to the Latest York Times, around half the expected votes will come on Election Day itself, making it difficult at this point to determine how significant a role early votes will play in the outcome.

#6806. Sacha Baron Cohen reveals “Who Is America?” and the answer is terrifying

📅 16 Jul 2018 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1875 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Salon ↗ Open Full Page

Sacha Baron Cohen reveals “Who Is America?” and the answer is terrifying

📅 16 Jul 2018 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1875 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Salon

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that showtime debuted Sacha Baron Cohen’s latest series on Sunday, finally providing a partial to the question its title poses.
  • Baron Cohen bases his career on that knowledge, but watching it in action was much more entertaining two decades ago in the heyday of “Da Ali G Show.” His HBO prank show became a cultural phenomenon before the omnipresence of social media and its accelerated mainstreaming of conspiracy theory as news, before a sitting president began making the denigration of objective journalism into a sport and before the proliferation of junk science as fact.
  • Back then cameras were not so prevalent as to persuade everyone that they were only one turned corner away from stardom.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that showtime debuted Sacha Baron Cohen’s latest series on Sunday, finally providing a partial to the question its title poses. “Who Is America?” The answer, on its face, will not surprise you: we are a nation of easy marks. Not merely easy, but willing.

Baron Cohen bases his career on that knowledge, but watching it in action was much more entertaining two decades ago in the heyday of “Da Ali G Show.” His HBO prank show became a cultural phenomenon before the omnipresence of social media and its accelerated mainstreaming of conspiracy theory as news, before a sitting president began making the denigration of objective journalism into a sport and before the proliferation of junk science as fact.

Back then cameras were not so prevalent as to persuade everyone that they were only one turned corner away from stardom. But today, being on camera is so natural and desirable to most of us that we are willing to say or do just about anything for a few of the 15 minutes we believe to be our birthright.

“Ali G” and the characters the show introduced, including Borat Sagdiyev and Brüno Gehard, also were born years before Project Veritas and InfoWars and other right-wing vehicles of disinformation made hidden camera hoaxing into something sinister.

All of which is to say, “Who Is America?” is not, as Showtime would like you to believe, “the most dangerous show in history.” At best, it is an occasionally funny one.

Recent findings suggest that but to anyone who mourns the collective deterioration of our population’s capacity to engage in critical thought, but has no idea of how urgent of a crisis that happens to be, Baron Cohen’s new endeavor is less of a comedy than a fright show. “Who Is America?” A nation of pliable dullards ripe for the hacking.

In a recent development, “Who Is America?” was produced in secret, and its pre-show marketing largely consisted of publicized declarations of outrage by such right-wing figures as Joe Walsh, Sarah Palin and Roy Moore. Each attempted to transform their extreme embarrassment at having been duped by a British clown hiding behind layers of latex and spirit gum into some approximation of righteous anger at remarked comedian’s dishonesty.

Showtime, meanwhile, maintained the aura of mystery surrounding the series almost to the brink of its debut, revealing the title only a little more than a week prior. The network released the briefest of clips featuring one famous interview subject, Dick Cheney.

This in itself was a bit of flimflam Showtime’s part: “Hope you’ll tune in next week for an interview with me,” Cheney states in the video, only to be a no-show in the premiere.

Sources indicate that you can’t blame “Who Is America?” for saving its biggest fish for later, because the famous politicians in the opener prove the problem of our collective gullibility just fine by themselves. In fact, although liberals may have gotten a hearty guffaw out of hearing Palin’s wailing about having been faked out by Baron Cohen, the very same character — Dr. Billy Wayne Ruddick Jr. PhD of Truthbrary.org — sat down for a conversation with none other than the honorable junior senator from Vermont, Bernie Sanders.

Sources indicate that prior to the premiere Billy Wayne tweeted a response to Palin’s accusation that he made fun disabled veterans. “I did NOT say I was a War Vet,” Ruddick’s “official” response reads, going on to explain that the service was in was “not military, but United Parcel”.

It has been revealed that nor does he make such assertions to Sanders, with whom he debates the merits of a universal healthcare proposal. And when I say debate, what I mean is that Sanders very calmly shares statistics with Billy Wayne long after the interviewer’s line of questioning stops making sense. And when Sanders asks Billy Wayne to confirm that he is disabled, given that he is conducting the interview while seated on a motorized scooter, Baron Cohen’s character replies that no, he is not. “This here scooter is to preserve my body’s finite energy,” Billy Wayne says.

READ MORE: That viral “strangers on a plane” Twitter story: Not a rom-com but a horror show.

One may be tempted to qualify Sanders’ appearance by pointing out that he acquitted himself well in the face of a person best be described as a few coconuts short of a beach vacation in Binomo.

Industry observers note that but this fails to answer the question of why Sanders signed a release, allowing this interview to be broadcast. Did anyone on Sanders’ team vet Truthbrary.org the moment Billy Wayne mentioned it? Even if they thought he was genuine, what is to be gained from being seen in a televised debate with a guy whose site includes a page titled  “Obamanoids — For Real!”?

According to recent reports, (To be fair, reportedly Baron Cohen almost fooled veteran news anchor Ted Koppel as part of his project. Koppel told The Hollywood Reporter that he was contacted to appear in a Showtime project titled “Age of Reason,” noted to feature “conversations with distinguished experts in science and public policy, highlighting the brightest and most reputable minds on today’s most important topics.” Koppel, perhaps receiving brainwaves from his colleague Sam Donaldson, wised up before Baron Cohen could pull him too deeply into his game.).

Recent findings suggest that A second character introduced in the premiere, an NPR shirt-wearing hyper-liberal named  Nira Cain-N’Degeocello, visits the opulent South Carolina home of wealthy Trump supporters he says are  “afflicted with white privilege.” But it soon becomes clear that his marks’ problem isn’t close-mindedness but over-correcting in the acceptance department. When Baron Cohen’s interviewer waxes on about encouraging his daughter Malala to “free bleed” on the American flag as a lesson, they simply nod and listen; when he chats about his wife’s ongoing affair with a dolphin, they don’t have any questions like, say, whether what they’re hearing is real.

This brings us to another answer to “Who Is America?”: we’re so aware of cameras, and desperate to have its focus upon us, that we will do and say anything without thinking of its possible permanence.

Demonstrating this is Baron Cohen’s third character Rick Sherman, an ex-con turned TV host who visits a Laguna Beach, California gallery to show his work, which is a series of capable but otherwise unextraordinary portraits rendered in feces and ejaculate.

Sources indicate that now, it’s entirely possible that the woman who runs the gallery might have been thinking she could have the next Andres Serrano on her hands. On the other hand, please.

This is a subject entirely aware of being on view, so obsessed with appearing erudite that while Rick is off camera, having excused himself to the facilities to commit another brown-and-white vision to paper, she addresses the camera like the host she was born to be.

“Who knew the world was capable of such oxymoronic paradoxical juxtapositions?” she muses. And this is before the homemade pubic hair paintbrush comes out.

In a recent development, baron Cohen has pushed the limits of tolerant everyday people many times in the past, mostly in a way that makes them look reasonable or, at the very least, more intelligent than the put-ons he inflicts upon them. And this is perhaps one of the most depressing aspects about “Who Is America?”, its demonstration of how endemic our lack of analysis truly is. I’m not saying that gallery owner is a stupid woman, understand.

But her interview is an example of prizing exposure over lasting consequence. By that I’m not merely referring to the fact that she placated a man who not only handed her pieces of cardboard purportedly smeared with his own dried excrement, or waited to receive a fresh sample of his work, but that she decided she needed to share her expert observation as to why she needed to do so by uttering a sentence full of five dollar words that add up to absolute nonsense.

In a recent development, (Either that or she’s a friend of Baron Cohen’s and in on the gag. I hope it’s option two, as opposed to her actually legitimizing the artistic relevance of number two.).

A number of reviews of “Who Is America?” have pointed out that Baron Cohen’s sneaky deceit is no longer funny because the formerly insane viewpoints Baron Cohen’s tactics expose have been normalized.

In a recent development, this has always been the danger, but it’s one every sort of parody or satire contends with in the current climate. It’s difficult to lampoon leaders seeking to legislate ludicrous patches to crises like gun violence instead of adopting common sense solutions like stricter regulation.

Which brings us to the portion of “Who Is America?” guaranteed to dominate Monday’s gallery of crazy clips, fronted by Baron Cohen’s Col. Erran Morad, a self-styled Israeli anti-terrorism expert who calls himself “the terrorist terminator.”.

The fake Mossad officer is there to promote his “Kinderguardians” program, a proposal that aims to train and arm toddlers in the classroom because, Moran says, arming teachers is crazy.

And this is the portion that has Walsh’s boxers in a bunch, because he joins House representatives Dana Rohrabacher and Joe Wilson in lending on-camera endorsements. Walsh’s comments are interwoven with a series of fake testimonials from the likes of Larry Pratt, executive director emeritus of the lobbying group Gun Owners of America and rape joke enthusiast.

Sources indicate that nobody forced Walsh to say, with gusto, “The way to stop a bad guy with is a good child with a gun. Happy shooting, kids!” If he didn’t want to say it, he wouldn’t have.

What Walsh might be upset about is being upstaged by Pratt, who earns some of the episode’s biggest laughs by reading the “science” behind the effectiveness of the fake program, revealing he doesn’t know the difference between human anatomy and hitmakers who grace Billboard’s pop charts.

Yes, “Who Is America?” gets mileage out of highlighting the callousness, sexism and extraordinary gullibility of conservatives, as Baron Cohen always has. But the things they say to him in disguise aren’t all that different than what they’d say on CNN, Fox, MSNBC or talk radio. Whatever power his comedy used to reveal is diminished by the fact that the charlatans no longer operate in secret.

According to recent reports, next week’s episode introduces one or two latest characters, although I don’t imagine they do anything more “dangerous” than the four we met on Sunday. For a number of viewers who love Baron Cohen’s schtick, that won’t matter.

To them “Who Is America?” is precisely on brand, showing Americans famous and everyday reacting to bizarre situations with varying degrees of what we consider to be normalcy in a time where the baseline version of normal is constantly morphing and shifting.

To other viewers, however, “Who Is America?” is a confirmation that Baron Cohen has run some tests and can confirm there is limited and ever decreasing brain activity in this worsening patient we know as America. It is something to behold, that’s for sure. But I’m not sure it’s the stuff of groundbreaking comedy. It’s not even really news.

#6803. Tech Report: “Borat 2” makes an America slathered in misogyny and disinformation reckon with itself
